basketball team|National team]]}} }} '''Džanan Musa''' ({{IPA|bs|d͡ʒânan mûsa}}, born 8 May 1999) is a Bosnian professional [[basketball]] player for [[Dubai Basketball]] of the [[ABA League]] and the [[EuroLeague]]. He also represents the senior [[Bosnia and Herzegovina men's national basketball team|Bosnia and Herzegovina national team]]. Standing at {{height|ft=6|in=9}} and weighing {{convert|215|lb|kg}}, Musa plays at the [[shooting guard]] and [[small forward]] positions. He was selected by the [[Brooklyn Nets]] with the 29th pick in the [[2018 NBA draft]]. ==Early career== Born in [[Bihać]], [[Bosnia and Herzegovina]], Musa began playing [[association football|soccer]] at first, before choosing to focus on basketball. Musa started playing junior basketball in the youth setup at KK Bosna XXL, when he was 8 years old. He then moved to [[Sarajevo]]-based KK Koš, before joining Croatian team [[KK Cedevita]] in 2014.{{cite web |author1=Federico Gaibotti |title=Eurotalents: Dzanan Musa, il prodigio di Bihac |url=https://www.basketuniverso.it/eurotalents-dzanan-musa-il-prodigio-di-bihac/ |website=basketuniverso.it |access-date=25 February 2019 |language=it |date=8 November 2016}} ==Professional career== ===Cedevita (2014–2018)=== In December 2014, he signed a deal with Croatian team [[KK Cedevita|Cedevita]].{{cite news|title=Cedevita Zagreb signs Dzanan Musa|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/croatia/145158/cedevita-zagreb-signs-bosnian-young-talent-dzanan-musa.html|access-date=17 December 2014|publisher=Sportando.com|date=17 December 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141219235235/http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/croatia/145158/cedevita-zagreb-signs-bosnian-young-talent-dzanan-musa.html|archive-date=19 December 2014|url-status=dead}} Musa made his debut in [[European professional club basketball system|Europe's top-tier]] level competition, the [[EuroLeague]], on 15 October 2015, making him [[List of youngest EuroLeague players since the 2000–01 season|the ninth-youngest player to make their debut in the EuroLeague]]. Musa played the first 4:55 minutes of the game and recorded 4 points.{{cite news|title=Sixteen-year-old Musa makes historic Euroleague debut for Cedevita|url=https://www.fiba.basketball/news/sixteen-year-old-musa-makes-historic-euroleague-debut-for-cedevita|archive-url=https://archive.today/20160403132054/http://www.fiba.com/news/sixteen-year-old-musa-makes-historic-euroleague-debut-for-cedevita|url-status=live|archive-date=3 April 2016|access-date=19 May 2016|publisher=FIBA.com|date=22 October 2015}} In June 2017, Musa attended the Adidas Eurocamp, a basketball camp based in [[Treviso]] for international [[NBA draft]] prospects.{{Cite news|url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/nba-news/460604/dzanan-musa-headlines-adidas-eurocamp/|title=Dzanan Musa headlines the Adidas Eurocamp|date=7 June 2017|access-date=12 April 2018|publisher=Eurohoops.net}} He was named the Eurocamp 2017 Most Improved Player.{{Cite news|url=http://www.nbadraft.net/dzanan-design|title=Dzanan Design|quote=He has already been praised for his improvement on D during 2017 Eurocamp (where he was chosen the most improved player) and showcased these skills during the tournament.|publisher=NBADraft.net|access-date=12 April 2018|date=9 July 2017|archive-date=24 June 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190624022629/https://www.nbadraft.net/dzanan-design|url-status=dead}} In the [[2017–18 EuroCup Basketball|2017–18 season]], while a member of [[KK Cedevita Junior|Cedevita]], Musa was awarded the [[EuroCup Basketball Rising Star|EuroCup Rising Star Trophy]], after averaging 10.5 points and 3.2 rebounds per game, in 16 selection.{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/usa/nba/271197/dzanan-musa-declares-for-the-2018-nba-draft.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180617015202/https://sportando.basketball/en/usa/nba/271197/dzanan-musa-declares-for-the-2018-nba-draft.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=17 June 2018|title=Dzanan Musa declares for the 2018 NBA Draft|date=12 April 2018|access-date=12 April 2018|publisher=Sportando.basketball}} On 21 June, he was selected with the 29th overall pick by the [[Brooklyn Nets]].{{cite web |last1=Dowd |first1=Tom |title=Brooklyn Nets Select Dzanan Musa, Rodions Kurucs in 2018 NBA Draft |url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/draft/2018/brooklyn-nets-select-dzanan-musa-rodions-kurucs-in-2018-nba-draft |website=NBA.com |access-date=3 October 2018 |date=22 June 2018}} On 12 July, the Nets signed Musa to a rookie scale contract.{{cite web |title=Brooklyn Nets Sign Dzanan Musa {{!}} Brooklyn Nets |url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/2018/07/12/brooklyn-nets-sign-dzanan-musa |website=NBA.com |access-date=3 October 2018 |date=12 July 2018}} During his rookie season, Musa had multiple assignments to the [[Long Island Nets]] of the [[NBA G League]].{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/assignments/|title=2018-19 NBA Assignments|work=NBA.com|access-date=9 November 2018}} On 19 November 2020, Musa was traded to the [[Detroit Pistons]] in a three-team trade.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/news/nets-acquire-shamet-from-clippers-in-3-team-trade|title=Nets acquire Shamet from Clippers in 3-team trade|work=NBA.com|date=19 November 2020|access-date=20 November 2020}} On 21 December 2020, Musa was waived by the Pistons.{{cite web|url=https://ca.sports.yahoo.com/news/detroit-pistons-waive-f-dzanan-192044416.html|title=Detroit Pistons waive F Dzanan Musa|work=[[Yahoo Sports]]|date=21 December 2020|access-date=21 December 2020|archive-date=17 February 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210217122911/https://ca.sports.yahoo.com/news/detroit-pistons-waive-f-dzanan-192044416.html|url-status=dead}} ===Anadolu Efes (2021)=== On 13 January 2021, Musa signed a 2.5 year contract with [[Anadolu Efes S.K.|Anadolu Efes]] of the [[Basketbol Süper Ligi|Turkish Basketball Super League]].{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/anadolu-efes-istanbul-signs-dzanan-musa-to-multi-year-deal/|title=Anadolu Efes Istanbul signs Dzanan Musa to multi-year deal|date=13 January 2021|newspaper=Sportando|language=En|access-date=13 January 2021 |last1=Carchia |first1=Emiliano }} On 27 June 2021, Efes used their option to exit from their mutual contract and Musa became a free agent. His short run with the Turkish club had four [[EuroLeague]] appearances and a short playing time total of 12 minutes. He also played in eight [[Basketball Super League|Turkish league]] games, averaging 11.4 points per game.{{cite web |last1=Askounis |first1=Johnny |title=Anadolu Efes releases Dzanan Musa |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/1223044/dzanan-musa-anadolu-efes-part-ways/ |website=Eurohoops |access-date=28 June 2021 |date=27 June 2021}} ===Río Breogán (2021–2022)=== On 21 July 2021, Musa signed with [[CB Breogán|Río Breogán]] of the [[Liga ACB]].{{cite news |title=Dzanan Musa joins CB Breogan |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/dzanan-musa-joins-cb-breogan/ |website=Sportando |access-date=22 July 2021 |date=21 July 2021 |last1=Skerletic |first1=Dario }} In just one season, Musa became one of Breogán's most legendary players, by helping them sealing participation in the [[Copa del Rey de Baloncesto|Copa del Rey]] for the first time in more than 30 years. Musa's best moments in a Breogán jersey include two games against [[Valencia Basket]], scoring 33 points with 44 [[Performance Index Rating|PIR]] and 31 points with 47 PIR, and a game-winner against Breogán's arch-rivals [[Obradoiro CAB|Obradoiro]]. He won several Player of the Week awards and two Player of the Month awards, and topped it off with the Liga ACB [[ACB Most Valuable Player Award|MVP of the Season]] award, which also made him the first Breogán player to ever win the most prestigious individual award in Spanish basketball.{{cite web |title=Dzanan Musa named ACB 2021-22 MVP |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/acb/1345793/dzanan-musa-named-acb-2021-22-mvp/ |website=Eurohoops |access-date=14 October 2023 |date=15 May 2022}} ===Real Madrid (2022–2025)=== On 14 July 2022, Musa signed a two-year deal with reigning Spanish champions and [[EuroLeague]] finalists [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]].{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2022/07/14/dzanan-musa-joins-real-madrid|title=Dzanan Musa joins Real Madrid|access-date=14 July 2022 |work=Real Madrid|date=14 July 2022}} In 2023, he played a crucial role in Real Madrid winning the 2023 EuroLeague Championship. He was named to the 2022-23 All-EuroLeague First Team.{{Cite web |date=2024-02-14 |title=DZANAN MUSA Profile {{!}} EuroLeague |url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/euroleague/players/dzanan-musa/profile/006540/ |access-date=2024-03-24 |website=Euroleague Basketball |language=en-GB}} On 8 July 2024, Musa renewed his contract with the Spanish powerhouse for an additional season.{{fact|date=August 2025}} ===Dubai Basketball (2025–present) === On 7 July 2025, Musa signed with [[Dubai Basketball]] of the [[ABA League]].{{Cite web|last1=Maggi |first1=Alessandro |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/dzanan-musa-is-officially-a-dubai-basketball-player/|title=Dzanan Musa is officially a Dubai Basketball player|work=Sportando |date=7 July 2025|language=En|access-date=7 July 2025}} ==National team career== Musa played at the [[2014 FIBA Europe Under-16 Championship]] with the Bosnian national Under-16 team, leading the tournament in scoring, at 23.0 points per game. He also played at the [[2015 FIBA Europe Under-16 Championship]], which he led in scoring, at 23.3 points per game, and in assisting, at 6.3 assists per game.{{cite web |title=2015 U16 European Championship Men |url=https://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/event/p/sID/11538/_/2015_U16_European_Championship_Men_Division_A/index.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180128090157/http://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/event/p/sid/11538/_/2015_U16_European_Championship_Men_Division_A/index.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=28 January 2018 |website=archive.fiba.com |access-date=3 October 2018}} He also averaged 9.0 rebounds per game, during the tournament. In the tournament's finals game, against the tournament's hosts, [[Lithuania men's national under-16 and under-17 basketball team|Lithuania]], Musa scored 33 points, to go along with his 8 rebounds, 7 assists, 3 steals and 2 blocks, leading his team to an 85–83 victory, and securing a gold medal for his team. Musa was named the [[2015 FIBA Europe Under-16 Championship#Awards|MVP of the tournament]], and he was also selected to the [[2015 FIBA Europe Under-16 Championship#Awards|All-Tournament Team]].{{cite web |title=2015 U16 European Championship Men - Final |url=https://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/game/p/gid/A/grid/72/rid/11555/sid/11538/_/2015_U16_European_Championship_Men/statistic.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924041105/http://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/game/p/gid/A/grid/72/rid/11555/sid/11538/_/2015_U16_European_Championship_Men/statistic.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=24 September 2015 |website=archive.fiba.com |access-date=3 October 2018}} Musa was named the [[2015 FIBA Europe Under-16 Championship#Awards|MVP of the tournament]], and he was also selected to the [[2015 FIBA Europe Under-16 Championship#Awards|All-Tournament Team]]. === U17 World Cup scoring record === Musa also played at the [[2016 FIBA Under-17 World Championship|2016 FIBA Under-17 World Cup]], which he led in scoring and in efficiency, with 34.0 points per game, and 27.7 efficiency per game and 194.0 overall. He also averaged 8.1 rebounds and 3.0 assists per game.{{cite web |title=Sexton takes 2016 FIBA U17 World Championship MVP honours, tops All-Star Five |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/world/u17/2016/news/sexton-takes-2016-fiba-u17-world-championship-mvp-honours-tops-all-star-five |website=FIBA.basketball |access-date=19 October 2022 |language=en |date=4 July 2016}}{{cite web |title=Dzanan MUSA at the FIBA U17 World Championship 2016 |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/world/u17/2016/player/Dzanan-Musa |website=FIBA.basketball |access-date=19 October 2022 |language=en}}{{cite web |title=Players statistics of the FIBA U17 World Championship 2016 |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/world/u17/2016/playerstats |website=FIBA.basketball |access-date=19 October 2022 |language=en}} During the tournament, Musa made history by breaking the record in most points scored in a single competitive game with 50 points in a game against Chinese Taipei, previous being 41 points and shared by Isaac Humphries and Jalen Howard, who scored his on 23 June, just six days earlier of Musa. On 29 June, Musa managed to shoot 18-of-26 from the field and 11-of-15 from the free-throw line, adding 7 rebounds and 4 assists during 27 minutes and 15 seconds he spent on court. This is the current record for the most points scored in a single game at the [[FIBA Under-17 World Cup]] tournament.{{cite web |title=After shedding tears of disappointment, Musa shatters scoring mark with 50 points |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/world/u17/2016/news/after-shedding-tears-of-disappointment-musa-shatters-scoring-mark-with-50-points |website=FIBA.basketball |access-date=19 October 2022 |language=en |date=29 June 2016}}{{cite web |title=Džanan Musa wrote history at U17 World Cup : ABA League |url=https://www.aba-liga.com/news/36649/dzanan-musa-wrote-history-at-u17-world-cup/ |website=ABA Liga j.t.d |access-date=19 October 2022 |language=en |date=29 June 2016}}{{cite web |title=Team
